items.headline: Dow jumps 3% for its best day since April 2025; S&P 500 +1.58%, Nasdaq +1.44%
items.note: Wednesday's rally followed Democratic wins in the House and Senate, which investors read as less political uncertainty, and U.S. crude fell more than 8%. The Dow closed at 53,356.12, up 1,569.40 points.

items.headline: Treasury yields ease as oil falls and divided government looks likelier
items.note: AP reported the 10-year yield slipping to about 4.89% from 4.95% the prior evening, as investors saw less risk of added federal borrowing. Lower oil also eased inflation worries, which matters because rate-hike fears have been weighing on stocks.

items.headline: AI stocks fall while the rest of the market rallies on data-center worries
items.note: Nvidia dropped about 3% and CoreWeave more than 7%, as investors worried about possible data-center restrictions, including a moratorium pledged by Texas's newly elected governor (per CNBC). The AI buildout is the demand behind many ML jobs and projects, so power and data-center policy is worth following.

items.headline: Apple hits an all-time high near $354, market cap above $5.12 trillion
items.note: Apple rose about 6% on Wednesday, a day after a margin warning hit the stock. CNBC says investors see it as less exposed to AI data-center spending than other big tech names.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO: no price range yet; earliest roadshow start is Nov 10
items.note: The S-1 was filed Oct 26 with the price range left blank; a range would appear in an amended filing. A report of trading before Thanksgiving is press speculation, not a confirmed schedule, and I found no amended filing today.

items.headline: Texas has paused data-center environmental permits pending a grid audit
items.note: Reports from September say Gov. Greg Abbott directed a suspension of data-center permit approvals until ERCOT finishes reviewing its interconnection queue. Sources disagree on exact dates, so treat it as background to this week's AI-infrastructure worries.

items.headline: McDonald's beats on earnings per share but misses on revenue
items.note: Adjusted EPS was $3.57 against a $3.38 estimate, but revenue of $7.16B missed the $7.29B forecast and U.S. same-store sales fell 0.2%. A handy example of a company 'beating' and still disappointing.

items.headline: Data science hiring is concentrated in big employers, with New York a top market
items.note: One analysis of U.S. postings (updated July 2026, not November) says New York has about 14% of data science postings and 49% come from employers with 10,000+ staff. General background, not new data.

learn.term: Price-weighted index (why the Dow moves in points)
learn.explain: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq weight companies by their total market value. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, with only 30 stocks, is price-weighted: a stock with a higher share price counts for more, no matter how big the company is. That's why headlines quote Dow moves in points. On Wednesday it rose 1,569.40 points, or 3.03%, to 53,356.12. The percentage is what lets you compare it with the S&P 500's 1.58% gain.
learn.try: Look up the 30 Dow components and find the stock with the highest share price, then compare its weight to its company's size.
